goal.intent: Contract checkers prove executable Actions semantics rather than matching workflow text

acceptance.acceptance: All three workflow verifiers reason over an Actions model in which comments and disabled jobs are not evidence

evidence.result: Only enabled steps of enabled jobs are evidence; YAML comments never reach the model and POSIX shell comments are stripped from run scripts with quoting state tracked.

acceptance.acceptance: Mutation tests fail closed for comment, if:false, wrong lane, non-executed scalar, renamed job, dropped matrix entry, relocated permission and YAML alias

evidence.result: Twenty mutations rejected: comment, shell comment, step name, if:false job, wrong lane, split step, renamed job, dropped matrix lane, overridden check name, path filter, relocated permission, blanket permission, branch push, workflow_dispatch, persist-credentials, anchor, alias, duplicate job key and duplicate step key.

acceptance.acceptance: Current workflows pass unchanged with no pin, permission or trigger weakened

evidence.result: All accept the unmodified workflows; exact pins, job permissions and triggers are asserted more strictly than before, never less.

acceptance.acceptance: The recorded comment-out mutations of the release identity step and the fuzz gate both fail the checkers

evidence.result: Both recorded reproductions now fail closed; before this change both left every checker exiting zero.

closure.summary: Merged as PR #54 after all four required checks passed on the exact head. The two recorded reproductions now fail closed, and twenty relocation and ambiguity mutations of the repository's own workflows are rejected while the unmodified workflows are accepted.

evidence.result: Merged to main with test (ubuntu-latest), test (macos-latest), govulncheck and Analyze (go) green.

closure.achieved_outcome: All three workflow contract verifiers reason over a parsed GitHub Actions model; a control that does not execute is not evidence.
closure.cleanup: Task branch deleted locally and on origin. Harness Serena state removed from the index and ignored, per the module anchor that disables it.

next_work.result: Now that workflow edits are guarded, bind the release receipt to an independently resolved commit and make the published schemas agree with the Go validators.

completeness_omission_audit.summary: A shell comment inside an executed run script was still counted, so demoting check-signature to a trailing comment survived the first model. Run scripts now have POSIX shell comments stripped with quoting state tracked, closing the last relocation the model missed.

evidence.result: Six cases pin the boundary, including hashes inside single and double quotes and a hash with no preceding whitespace, which must all stay executable text.

execute.summary: Added internal/actions with the workflow model, shell-comment-aware run scripts and fail-closed parsing. Rewrote the cicontract, releasecontract and governance verifiers against it, adding per-lane pin counting, persist-credentials, trigger, permission-scope, matrix-lane and check-name assertions that text matching could not express.

evidence.result: All four contract checkers accept the unmodified workflows; the module closure stayed at six modules and twelve go.sum lines.

gap_plan.summary: Adopt github.com/goccy/go-yaml and build internal/actions, a narrow Actions model in which only enabled steps of enabled jobs are evidence. Reject anchors, aliases and duplicate keys rather than approximate them. Rewrite all three verifiers against it and add mutation tests on the relocation axis the previous suite never covered.

evidence.result: goccy/go-yaml v1.19.2 is a single module with zero transitive go.sum entries and detects duplicate keys by default; gopkg.in/yaml.v3 was rejected because its pre-pruning go.mod drags gopkg.in/check.v1 into the pinned closure

orient.summary: Three workflow verifiers matched text: releasecontract used strings.Contains, cicontract global strings.Count, governance a hand-rolled indentation parser. None built an Actions model, so a required command preserved in a comment, a disabled job, another lane or a non-executed scalar still counted as present.

evidence.reference: commented out the release identity step in .github/workflows/release.yml
evidence.result: check-ci-contract, check-release-contract and check-governance-contract all exited 0 while the signature, provenance and exact-main gate was absent from the parsed job

reconcile.summary: Adding the parser dependency propagated to release/v1alpha1.json, the release-contract schema and the Go licence rule, which was a single BSD-3-Clause constant. Widened it to a closed allowlist rather than removing the check.

evidence.result: release contract valid: v0.1.3, five source/module assets, Go 1.25; the dependency closure now names github.com/goccy/go-yaml v1.19.2 under MIT.

self_review.summary: Three pre-existing negative fixtures were passing for the wrong reason: they appended the forbidden token as a trailing YAML comment, which weakens nothing. Rewrote them to place the forbidden command in an executed run script, and added a staleness guard that fails when a mutation stops changing the workflow.

evidence.result: clobber, ambient Git trust and direct Git verifier now mutate the gh release create invocation and the identity script; each fails closed and each asserts it actually changed the file.

verify.summary: gofmt, go vet, staticcheck v0.7.0, the full suite under umask 002, race, all six contract checkers, and a deterministic double release build compared byte for byte.

evidence.result: All green. Twenty relocation and ambiguity mutations of the real workflows are rejected and the unmodified workflows are accepted.
